title: Sparse checkpoint rollback advisor with batched warmup and state repair
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build an automated rollback advisor that uses sparse checkpointing and a batched warmup phase to safely apply or revert config changes that affect batching and caching. The advisor should combine predictive cost signals (token / throughput delta estimates), safety heuristics, and a compact state-repair plan to reconcile KV cache and serving state after rollbacks. The feature targets production config changes that modify batching parameters, cache eviction policies, kernel selection toggles, and autoscaler thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: Advisor can evaluate a proposed config diff and produce a safety score (safe | cautious | unsafe) with an explanation of dominant signals
For changes marked cautious, the advisor suggests a sparse-checkpoint plan: (snapshot keys to preserve, light-weight warmup traffic pattern) and an estimated cost delta

Automated canary apply triggers batched warmup traffic and tracks a small set of telemetry metrics (latency P95, throughput, cache hit ratio, cost per token); failure beyond thresholds auto-triggers the rollback plan
Rollback plan includes an idempotent state-repair stepset that reconciles prefix KV-caches and replays missing warmup prefixes without full cold start
End-to-end e2e tests and a staging runbook exist and demonstrate rollback recoveries under synthetic workload regressions
steps: Design: finalize safety signals and scoring rubric (cost delta, cache-hit impact, latency delta, error-rate delta)
Proto: implement sparse checkpoint format and lightweight snapshotter for serving state
Advisor: implement scoring service and explainability strings for suggested actions
Apply: integrate canary apply with batched warmup harness that feeds reproducible traffic patterns
Rollback: implement state-repair routines and verify idempotency
Observability: add a per-change dashboard (telemetry + explanation + suggested mitigation)
QA: run chaos scenarios in staging (cache regressions, partial warmup failures, noisy traffic)
Doc: write operator runbook and console UX copy for suggested rollback steps
design_decisions: Use sparse checkpointing (only store keys/metadata needed to rehydrate common prefixes) to limit snapshot size and speed up rollbacks
Perform warmup as batched micro-sessions to quickly rebuild hot KV entries without impacting production latency SLOs
Score combines economic and reliability signals; safety score tuned to prefer rollback if cost>10% AND cache-hit-drop>8% over 15 minutes
Make state-repair idempotent and bounded (cap on number of prefix replay attempts) to avoid runaway recovery traffic
Separate advisor evaluation from apply execution — advisor returns human-readable recommendations and a machine-actionable plan
rollout_plan: Start with internal infra namespace in staging, run 20 synthetic canaries per day for 2 weeks, gradually enable advisor suggestions in console as 'recommend only' for a pilot set of teams, then enable automated guarded apply/rollback for low-risk change classes. Monitor cost and SLO deltas and maintain a quickkill toggle for manual overrides.
testing_plan: Unit tests for scoring logic covering edge cases (zero-cost changes, noisy telemetry)
Integration test: sparse checkpoint create/restore under simulated memory pressure
E2E canary test: inject a config that reduces batch size and verify advisor suggests rollback with correct explanation
Chaos test: force a partial warmup failure and validate rollback state-repair idempotency
Performance test: measure snapshotting overheads on a 2000-QPS serving pool
risks_mitigations: Risk: false positives cause unnecessary rollbacks -> Mitigation: require multi-signal agreement and a short cool-down before auto-rollback
Risk: rollback traffic overloads cold caches -> Mitigation: batched warmup pattern throttles rebuilds and prioritizes hot prefixes
Risk: opaque advisor explanations reduce trust -> Mitigation: include per-signal contribution scores and links to raw telemetry
Risk: state-repair may not cover vendor-specific cache encodings -> Mitigation: provide pluggable repair adapters per serving runtime
